claim: ADR 0340 rule 26 (§F13), lane 6b: getOnboardingProgress in apps/api-gateway/src/menus/menus.service.ts reads the house's live lines through readCurrentMenuLines(..., { drinks: true }) and sets menu_current (the menu half of activated) only when at least one row comes back; readCurrentMenuLines in current-menu-lines.ts keeps a row only when lineIsDrink says so on its own menu's kind. So a house whose only live menu is Food is not activated, and a failed read of restaurant_menus or menu_items throws. The verify reads the method body and the helper by text (comments stripped); two-kinds-live.spec.ts drives the Food-only, dessert-wine and failed-read cases. It does not prove the readers that build the onboarding checklist elsewhere use the same rule

ADR 0340 rules 13, 18 and 20, lane 6b: the first proof at /house/menu (apps/web/src/pages/HouseMenu.tsx, the first-run review since ADR 0213) hands its one MenuPlan every draft of a read split by kind that is not live yet (the first as menuId, the rest as batchIds), so one tap reviews and makes them live together, and a kind the plan left a draft is offered again; a read that was not split passes its one menu as before. The verify reads the component's text with line comments dropped; ArrivalFlow.test.tsx drives it. It does not cover several files read at once (MenuCsvUpload merges them into one proof whose drafts are the first file's)
verify: python3 -c "import re,sys; t=open('apps/web/src/pages/HouseMenu.tsx').read(); t=re.sub(r'(?m)^[ \t]*//[^\n]*\n', '', t); w=' '.join(t.split()); ok='const drafts = useMemo(() => proofDrafts(proof?.drafts), [proof])' in w and 'const pending = liveIds ? drafts.filter((d) => !liveIds.includes(d.menuId)) : []' in w and 'menuId={split ? pending[0].menuId : proof.menuId}' in w and 'batchIds={split ? pending.slice(1).map((d) => d.menuId) : undefined}' in w and w.count('<MenuPlan ')==1; sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)"
